title: Continuum Backup & Recovery Service Delivery Terms — Seeding, Activation and Protected Devices
content:
Seeding of a Continuum Backup & Recovery plan starts once the order is signed; the tier's seeding target in calendar days is a target. The plan activates when every contracted server has a verified full backup, the term starting on the activation date and ending the day before the same day of the month the term's number of months later; activation grants the first year's cloud failover server-days included annually on the tier. An order may be cancelled by the client only before seeding starts, the onboarding fee then being reversed.

Items are protected and unprotected one at a time by hostname or user sign-in; protection changes may be posted only while the plan status is seeding, active, suspended or notice given. Scheduled server backups run at the tier's backup interval; the immutable cloud copy, the on-site backup appliance, backup-stream anomaly detection, around-the-clock triage of failed backups with remediation of a failed backup started within the tier's remediation-start time as a target, and the tier's backup report cadence are entitlements of the tier. Removing an item never generates a credit for the current month, and its restore points remain until they age out under the tier's retention days.

## From order to active term

| Plan status | What it means |
|---|---|
| ordered | The client has signed an order for a Continuum tier, server commitment and term; seeding has not begun |
| seeding | Initial full backups (seeding) of the protected devices have begun |
| active | Seeding is verified complete and the term has started |
| cancelled | The client cancelled the order before seeding began |

The activation condition is that every contracted server — every server of the server commitment on the order — has a verified full backup. The seeding target does not itself activate the plan.

## The term dates

The term starts on the activation date. It ends on the day before the same day of the month that falls the term's number of months later.

**Worked dates (hypothetical).**

| Activation date | Term | Same day of the month, term later | Last day of the term |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10th of a month | 12 months | 10th of the same month one year later | 9th of that month |
| 10th of a month | 36 months | 10th of the same month three years later | 9th of that month |
| 10th of a month | 1 month | 10th of the following month | 9th of the following month |

## Order cancellation

| When the client cancels | Outcome under this clause |
|---|---|
| While the plan status is ordered, before seeding starts | The order may be cancelled; the onboarding fee is reversed |
| After seeding has started | The client may not cancel the order under this clause |

## Protecting and unprotecting items

Each protected server, workstation or Microsoft 365 user is added or removed individually, identified by its hostname or user sign-in, with its class and the date protection started or stopped. The plan's count of protected devices is the servers, workstations and Microsoft 365 users currently protected under it: an item protected raises it by one and an item unprotected lowers it by one.

| Plan status, as shown on the plan record | May a protection change be posted? |
|---|---|
| seeding | Yes |
| active | Yes |
| suspended | Yes |
| notice given | Yes |
| ordered | No |
| closed | No |
| cancelled | No |

## Removing an item

When an item is removed, no credit is generated for the current month, and its existing restore points stay until they age out under the tier's retention days. For example, on a hypothetical tier retaining restore points for 30 days, a workstation removed today keeps each existing restore point until that point is 30 days old.
